newsitem.title: USA: U.S. pork production seen flat in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pork production seen flat in 1997.

text.p: U.S. pork production will be little changed in 1997 from the prior year, laying the groundwork for a pickup in 1998 and 1999, U.S. Agriculture Department livestock analyst James Nix said.

"Pork production will probably rise sharply in 1998 after wallowing along this year at about the 1996 level," Nix said in a speech prepared for delivery on Tuesday at USDA's annual Agricultural Outlook Forum.
He said pork output in the first half of 1997 would drop about two percent but that output could gain five percent in the third quarter and end the year with a flat fourth quarter.
Nix said pork production was expected to rise "substantially" in 1998, perhaps as much as six to eight percent, with increases continuing but moderating in 1999.

Nix forecast 1997 hog prices would average a couple of dollars above the 1996 level but said a sharp drop in prices is likely in 1998 when production increases. Prices in 1999 will also be under the pressure of large supplies.

"A supporting factor for prices in 1998 and 1999 will be a lot less competition from beef, but it remains to be seen just how much this might be offset by increased poultry output," Nix said in the speech.
